This document presents a comprehensive, feat-by-feat intelligence analysis of Light Yagami (Kira) as portrayed in the first eighteen chapters of the Death Note fan fiction "God of The New World," written by u/AnnualFrequent7426 and u/Last-Trainer-333. The analysis employs the SCD (Smart Character Discussion) methodology, a community-driven framework developed on Reddit for the rigorous, comparative assessment of fictional character intelligence. The SCD approach draws inspiration from the WAIS (Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale), adapting its index-based structure for fictional analysis while expanding far beyond standardized testing into the domains of strategic thinking, psychological manipulation, deception, social intelligence, and adversarial reasoning.

Every single intelligence feat performed by Light Yagami across the eighteen chapters has been extracted, categorized, and scored on a 1-10 comparative scale. Complex feats, those involving multi-layered strategies, significant psychological warfare, or operationally sophisticated methodology, receive detailed breakdowns covering context, objective, methodology, reasoning process, psychological warfare elements, and outcome. Simpler feats receive condensed summaries with their relevant SCD category tags and scores. The scoring is comparative, meaning a score of 10 in a given subcategory represents the theoretical ceiling of what a fictional character of this type has demonstrated in SCD discussions, not an absolute standard.

The taxonomy encompasses 16 primary categories with over 100 subcategories: Strategy (11 sub), Planning (10 sub), Manipulation (12 sub), Deception (6 sub), Thinking (11 sub), Reasoning (8 sub), Foresight (3 sub), Emotional Intelligence (6 sub), Social Intelligence (8 sub), Adversity Capacity (6 sub), Insight (9 sub), Field Skills (7 sub), Adaptability (5 sub), Psychology (8 sub), Counteraction (3 sub), and Countering (5 sub). WAIS-inspired composite indices (VCI, PRI, EI) are calculated at the document's conclusion to provide a holistic intelligence profile.

A total of 70 distinct intelligence feats were identified and extracted from the first eighteen chapters. Of these, 19 were classified as complex feats receiving full detailed breakdowns, and 51 were classified as simple feats receiving condensed summaries with category tags and scores. The feats span every major intelligence domain, from grand strategic planning (the Fake Russian Profile misdirecting every intelligence agency on Earth) to micro-level emotional manipulation (the Benjamin Franklin Effect on Naomi Misora) to operational ingenuity under impossible conditions (the Chips Bag System enabling kills while under 58-camera surveillance).

Two experiments: (1) Otoharada Kurou, specifying suicide by gunshot, with 40-second observation window. (2) Shibumaru Takuo, written 7 times with different kanji pronunciations, specifying traffic accident. Each test isolates a variable to verify the mechanism.

Feat 4-1: Triple-Layer Hide System with Incendiary Trap

Creates a hide-within-a-hide-within-a-hide for the Death Note: Layer 1 is a mundane diary decoy; Layer 2 is the Death Note under a false bottom activated by inserting a pen in a hidden hole; Layer 3 is an incendiary trap with gasoline bag and circuit that ignites if opened incorrectly, destroying all evidence.

L is the world's greatest detective and may search Light's room at any time. The Death Note must be both undetectable and destroyable in emergencies.
Create a multi-layered defense system that handles different threat levels: casual searchers (Layer 1), skilled investigators (Layer 2), and forced entry (Layer 3).

(1) Mundane diary on top as first line of defense, stopping anyone who isn't specifically looking for something hidden. (2) False bottom requiring specific technique to open: inserting a pen through a hidden hole to separate metal plates. (3) Incendiary system: gasoline bag + electrical circuit that closes if the compartment is forced open, creating a spark that ignites the gasoline and destroys the notebook.
(4) Cover story for the system: 'I just didn't want anyone reading my real diary.
Defense in depth. Each layer addresses a different threat model. The incendiary layer is the ultimate failsafe: even if all other layers fail, the evidence is destroyed.
The cover story ('protecting diary privacy') is plausible and relatable, so even if the mechanism is discovered, the purpose seems innocent.
The incineration plan itself has a cover story. Light understands that the mechanism of hiding can be as incriminating as what is hidden, so he provides a benign explanation for the entire system.
Multi-threat defense operational. Never actually triggered, but its existence demonstrates Light's commitment to operational security at every level.
